Advanced TypeScript Features - Part 3

January 20, 2024 by Test Author 1 min read

Advanced TypeScript Features

Welcome to the final part of our TypeScript Fundamentals series! Let's explore some advanced features.

Generics

Generics allow you to create reusable components that work with multiple types:

function identity<T>(arg: T): T {
  return arg;
}

let output1 = identity<string>("hello");
let output2 = identity<number>(42);

// Generic interfaces
interface Box<T> {
  value: T;
}

let stringBox: Box<string> = { value: "hello" };
let numberBox: Box<number> = { value: 42 };

Utility Types

TypeScript provides several utility types:

interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
}

// Partial - makes all properties optional
type PartialUser = Partial<User>;

// Pick - selects specific properties
type UserPreview = Pick<User, "id" | "name">;

// Omit - removes specific properties
type UserWithoutEmail = Omit<User, "email">;

// Readonly - makes all properties readonly
type ReadonlyUser = Readonly<User>;

Decorators

Decorators provide a way to add annotations and meta-programming syntax:

function log(target: any, propertyKey: string, descriptor: PropertyDescriptor) {
  const originalMethod = descriptor.value;

  descriptor.value = function(...args: any[]) {
    console.log(`Calling ${propertyKey} with`, args);
    return originalMethod.apply(this, args);
  };
}

class Calculator {
  @log
  add(a: number, b: number): number {
    return a + b;
  }
}

Conclusion

Congratulations! You've completed the TypeScript Fundamentals series. You now have a solid foundation to build amazing TypeScript applications.
